definition_zh: 创新；革新；（新）方法、新事物
definition_en: a new idea, method, or product, or the act of creating such new things
core_image: 旧机器旁边摆出一台从没见过的新装置，围着看的人抄下了图纸
scene: 老厂房里摆着一排用了多年的旧设备，墙角却多了一台新样机。The engineer called the new design a real innovation, not just a small repair.
sceneCN: 这里 innovation 是「创新、新东西」（第 1 个义项：全新的想法、方法或产品），句意为工程师说这项新设计是真正的创新，而不只是一次小修小补。画面里的物件：旧设备、新样机、图纸。

derivatives.zh: 由本词换后缀构成，义为「创新的；有新意的」
由拉丁词干构成的后备动词，义为「革新；创新」
由本词加 -or 构成，义为「创新者；革新者」
由本词加 -al 构成，义为「与创新有关的」

senses.title: A new idea or method
senses.definition: a new idea, method, or device, especially one that changes how something is done
senses.definitionCN: 尤指改变了做事方式的新想法、新方法或新装置
senses.example: The online booking system was a real innovation for the small hotel.
senses.exampleCN: 网上预订系统对这家小旅馆来说是真正的创新。
senses.why: Latin novus means new; in- makes it "into the new", so an innovation is something brought into the world as new.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 novus 意为「新的」；in- 使之成为「进入新奇状态」，所以 innovation 是被带进世界的新东西。

senses.title: The act of bringing in new things
senses.definition: the activity of introducing new ideas or methods into a business, school, or industry
senses.definitionCN: 把新想法或新方法引入企业、学校或行业的行为
senses.example: Innovation is what keeps a small company alive in a crowded market.
senses.exampleCN: 创新是让小公司在拥挤的市场中活下来的东西。
senses.why: The noun also names the doing, not only the thing done: it is the process of stepping into the new.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词也指「做的过程」而不只是「做成的东西」：它就是走进新事物的过程。

senses.title: A new product on the market
senses.definition: a product or service that is new to the market and often credited to one company
senses.definitionCN: 市场上新出现、往往归功于某家公司的新产品或新服务
senses.example: Their latest innovation is a battery that charges in minutes.
senses.exampleCN: 他们最新的革新产品是一种几分钟就能充满电的电池。
senses.why: From the busy workshop it moved to the shop window: each launch is presented as an innovation.
senses.whyCN: 从忙碌的车间走到了橱窗：每一次新品发布都被称为一项 innovation。

senses.title: A change in long-standing habits
senses.definition: a change in well-established customs or habits, sometimes unwelcome at first
senses.definitionCN: 对由来已久的习惯或风俗所做的改变，起初常不受欢迎
senses.example: Replacing the paper register with an app was an innovation nobody asked for.
senses.exampleCN: 用一个应用取代纸质登记簿，是没人要求过的改变。
senses.why: The oldest examples refer to novelties in religion and law, where a new practice always disturbed someone.
senses.whyCN: 最早的例子指宗教与法律上的新做法，新的做法总会惊动某些人。

intro.en: Innovation is a Latin noun of action built on novus "new"; English took it through French in the Middle Ages.
intro.cn: innovation 是以拉丁语 novus「新的」为基础的拉丁语行为名词，中世纪经法语进入英语。

items.en: The adjective novus "new" is old Latin and related to the adverb novus-derived nunc "now".
items.cn: 形容词 novus「新的」是古老的拉丁词，与表示「现在」的 nunc 有渊源。

items.en: Novare "to make new" yielded the verb innovare, literally "to make new in".
items.cn: novare「使变新」生出动词 innovare，字面是「使里面变新」。

items.en: The abstract noun innovatio "a renewing" was used in late Latin, chiefly for renewal of laws.
items.cn: 抽象名词 innovatio「更新」见于晚期拉丁语，主要用于法律的更新。

items.en: Old French innovacion carried the word into everyday speech during the Middle Ages.
items.cn: 中世纪时古法语 innovacion 把这个词带入日常言语。

items.en: From the sixteenth century it named any new practice; business writing later made it a slogan.
items.cn: 十六世纪起它泛指任何新做法；后来的商业写作又让它成为口号。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the Latin root for "new"; the near-meaning group holds other words for change and novelty.
note.cn: 形近组共享拉丁语「新」这一词根；近义组收其他表示「改变、新事物」的词。

entries.definition: A story; as an adjective, new and unusual, built on Latin novus.
entries.definitionCN: 名词义为「小说」，作形容词义为「新颖的」，都基于拉丁语 novus。

entries.definition: The quality of being new, or a small new object sold for fun.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「新奇；新奇小玩意」，词根同是「新」。

entries.definition: To make an old building new again, with the prefix re- "again".
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「翻新」，前缀 re- 表「再次」，词根仍是「新」。

entries.definition: Something created for the first time, often a device.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「发明」，指首次创造出的东西，常指装置。

entries.definition: A change that repairs a system rather than creating something new.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「改革」，指修补制度而非创造新事物。

entries.definition: A sudden important advance, stronger in tone than innovation.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「突破」，语气比 innovation 更强，强调突然的重要进展。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the Latin root nov- "new" and the phrases the word really appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子利用拉丁词根 nov-「新」以及这个词真实的搭配。

normal.en: nov- is new: innovation is the new thing brought in.
normal.cn: nov- 就是「新」：innovation 就是被带进来的新东西。

normal.en: The same root gives novel, novelty and renovate.
normal.cn: 同一词根给出 novel、novelty、renovate。

normal.en: Tech firms live or die by technological innovation.
normal.cn: 科技公司的生死取决于技术创新。

normal.en: An innovation is judged by users, not by its inventor.
normal.cn: 创新由用户评判，而不是由发明者评判。

normal.en: Small innovations often beat one big invention.
normal.cn: 许多小创新往往胜过一件大发明。

abstract.en: Think of a door marked in- that opens into a room called new.
abstract.cn: 想象一扇标着 in- 的门，通向一个叫「新」的房间。

abstract.en: An innovation is a habit the world has not yet learned.
abstract.cn: 创新是世界尚未学会的一种习惯。

abstract.en: Every innovation starts as someone else's odd idea.
abstract.cn: 每一项创新最初都是别人眼里的怪想法。

examples.en: The factory owes its survival to steady innovation.
examples.cn: 这家工厂靠持续创新才得以存活。

examples.en: Cheap solar panels were the decade's biggest innovation.
examples.cn: 廉价太阳能板是那十年最大的创新。

examples.en: Teachers were asked to share one innovation at the meeting.
examples.cn: 会上要求老师们各分享一项创新做法。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「一脑维新」——一脑子的维新想法，就是创新

root: 拉丁语 novus「新的」→ novare「使变新」→ innovare「使里面变新」→ 晚期拉丁语抽象名词 innovatio「更新」，中世纪经古法语 innovacion 进入英语。nov-「新」也见于 novel、novelty、renovate。

sensesIntro.en: Four senses: the new thing, the act of making it, the product sold, and the change imposed on old habits.
sensesIntro.cn: 四个义项：新东西本身、制造新东西的行为、售卖的新产品，以及强加于旧习惯的改变。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: something never seen before is brought in and set beside the old.
core.cn: 核心意象：一件从未见过的东西被带进来，摆在旧东西旁边。

branches.en: THE WORKSHOP: a new method enters the way work is done.
branches.cn: 车间这条线：新方法进入做事的流程。

branches.en: THE PROCESS: innovation also names the ongoing act of bringing new things in.
branches.cn: 过程这条线：innovation 也指持续把新东西带进来的行为。

branches.en: THE SHOP WINDOW: the product itself is displayed as an innovation.
branches.cn: 橱窗这条线：产品本身被展示为一项创新。

branches.en: THE OLD CUSTOM: a change in habit is resisted before it is accepted.
branches.cn: 旧风俗这条线：习惯的改变先被抵制，之后才被接受。

branches.en: THE LINK: the thing and the act share the movement into the new.
branches.cn: 连接线：东西与行为共享「走进新」这一动作。

intro.en: Innovation splits into the Latin prefix in-, the root nov- "new", and the noun ending -ation.
intro.cn: innovation 可拆为拉丁前缀 in-、「新」词根 nov- 与名词词尾 -ation。

latinIntro.en: Latin novus, novare and innovare are all attested, so only the deeper Indo-European form is reconstructed.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 novus、novare、innovare 均有记载，只有更早的印欧形式属于重构。

items.example: It marks the movement towards the new state.
items.exampleCN: 它标出朝向新状态的动作。

items.example: The root is visible in novel and renovate.
items.exampleCN: 这一词根见于 novel 与 renovate。

items.example: The adjective is the base of the whole family.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词是整个词族的根基。

items.example: It turns the adjective into an action.

items.meaning: to renew, bring in new things
items.example: The compound gave the French and English noun.
items.exampleCN: 这个复合动词给出法语与英语的名词。

items.example: It makes the word an abstract noun.
items.exampleCN: 它使这个词成为抽象名词。

items.example: The verb is back-formed from the noun.
The suffix marks the quality.

latinEntries.meaning: to renew, bring in new things

definition_zh: 输入；投入（资源、意见）；输入端；输入数据
definition_en: something put into a system, such as data, effort, or money, or the act of putting it in
core_image: 一只手把数据卡片推进机器的进料口
scene: 技术员坐在电脑前核对屏幕上的一行行数字。The new software needs less input from the user.
sceneCN: 这里 input 是「输入」（第 1 个义项：输入系统的数据或指令）；句意为新软件需要的用户输入更少。图中可辨识物件：键盘、屏幕、数据卡。

pos.zh: 名词：输入；投入；输入端；输入数据

derivatives.zh: 由本词加 device 构成，义为「输入设备」
由本词加后缀构成，义为「数据录入」
由前缀 out- 构成的对应词，义为「输出」

senses.title: Data put into a computer
senses.definition: information or instructions put into a computer or a machine
senses.definitionCN: 送入计算机或机器的信息或指令
senses.example: The program waits for input from the keyboard.
senses.exampleCN: 程序等待来自键盘的输入。
senses.why: Input is the noun of putting in: whatever is pushed into a system through its entrance.
senses.whyCN: input 是「put in」的名词：凡经入口推送进系统的东西。

senses.title: Effort or resources put in
senses.definition: the effort, money, advice, or time given to a project, often by several people
senses.definitionCN: 投入某项工程的努力、资金、建议或时间，常由多方提供
senses.example: The report was written with input from every department.
senses.exampleCN: 这份报告是在各部门的意见基础上写成的。
senses.why: Factories speak of inputs of labour and materials, and meetings of inputs of advice.
senses.whyCN: 工厂说劳动与材料的投入，会议说建议的投入。

senses.title: The terminal that receives data
senses.definition: a place or device through which signals enter a system
senses.definitionCN: 信号进入系统的位置或装置
senses.example: Plug the cable into the audio input.
senses.exampleCN: 把线插进音频输入口。
senses.why: The entrance point takes the name of what passes through it.
senses.whyCN: 入口处往往就以流经它的东西命名。

intro.en: Input is not Latin at all: it is put with the prefix in- on the English model of output.
intro.cn: input 完全不是拉丁词：它是英语把 put 加前缀 in- 造出的词，与 output 对应。

items.en: Put has no certain origin even in Old English, where it appears in place names.
items.cn: put 连在古英语中也来源不明，只在地名里出现。

items.en: Input was formed in the eighteenth century for money and resources put into a business.
items.cn: input 在十八世纪造出，指投入企业的资金与资源。

items.en: Engineers took up the word for power and signals feeding a machine.
items.cn: 十九世纪工程师用它指供给机器的动力与信号。

items.en: Computing fixed the sense of data entered into a system, and output grew beside it.
items.cn: 计算机业固定了「输入数据」的义项，output 随之而来。

items.en: Everyday speech extended it to advice and effort contributed by people.
items.cn: 日常用语又把它扩展到人们贡献的意见与努力。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words made with put and with the prefix in-; the near-meaning group gathers other words for contributions.
note.cn: 形近组收由 put 与 in- 构成的词；近义组收表示「贡献」的其他词。

entries.definition: What a system produces, the opposite of input.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「输出」，与 input 相对。

entries.definition: The act of entering data.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「数据录入」，由本词构成。

entries.definition: To bring goods into a country, with a Latin root.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「进口」，形近但词源不同。

entries.definition: Something given to a shared effort.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「贡献」，指对共同努力的付出。

entries.definition: Information in a form a computer can process.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「数据」，指可供计算机处理的信息。

entries.definition: Money or effort put in for future gain.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「投资」，指为将来收益而投入的钱或力。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the plain English build of the word, which is simply in plus put.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子利用这个词朴素的英语构成，即 in 加 put。

normal.en: Input is in plus put: what you put in.
normal.cn: input 就是 in 加 put：你投入进去的东西。

normal.en: Output sits on the other side of the same wall.
normal.cn: output 位于同一堵墙的另一侧。

normal.en: Ask for input before you write the report, not after.
normal.cn: 写报告之前征求意见，别等后面。

normal.en: Users type input; the computer answers with output.
normal.cn: 用户键入 input，计算机回以 output。

normal.en: An audio input is the socket that lets sound in.
normal.cn: audio input 是让声音进来的插孔。

abstract.en: Picture grain poured into a hopper: what goes in determines what comes out.
abstract.cn: 想象谷物倒进料斗：送进去的决定了出来的。

abstract.en: A system is only as good as the input it receives.
abstract.cn: 系统的质量取决于它接收的输入。

abstract.en: Every effort you put in is a kind of input, even when nobody records it.
abstract.cn: 你的每一点付出都是一种输入，即使没人记录。

examples.en: The form asks for input of your personal details.
examples.cn: 表格要求输入你的个人信息。

examples.en: We would welcome input from parents on the new timetable.
examples.cn: 新课程表方面我们欢迎家长提出意见。

examples.en: Insert the microphone into the input at the back.
examples.cn: 把麦克风插到后面的输入口。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「因普特」——因「普特」把数据输入了电脑

root: input 是英语用 in- + put 仿 output 构成的词，十八世纪指投入企业的资金与资源；十九世纪用于机器动力与信号，二十世纪计算机业固定为「数据输入」，后引申为「意见投入」。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses: data entering a machine, resources or advice entering a project, and the socket where signals enter.
sensesIntro.cn: 三个义项：进入机器的数据、进入项目的资源与意见，以及信号进入的接口。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: grain is poured into a hopper; what goes in decides what comes out.
core.cn: 核心意象：谷物倒进料斗，进多少决定出多少。

branches.en: THE KEYBOARD: typing is the commonest form of input.
branches.cn: 键盘这条线：打字是最常见的 input。

branches.en: THE PROGRAM: a program cannot run without data from somewhere.
branches.cn: 程序这条线：没有数据来源，程序无法运行。

branches.en: THE MEETING: a good decision needs input from the people affected.
branches.cn: 会议这条线：好的决定需要受影响者的意见。

branches.en: THE FACTORY: labour, fuel and material are the inputs of production.
branches.cn: 工厂这条线：劳动、燃料与材料是生产的投入。

branches.en: THE SOCKET: the input is also the physical entrance.
branches.cn: 接口这条线：the input 也指物理上的入口。

intro.en: Input is a modern English compound; the prefix in- carries the sense of entering.
intro.cn: input 是现代英语复合词，前缀 in- 承载「进入」之意。

latinIntro.en: The form looks Latin but is English; the table records the native and Latin-related elements honestly.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词形似拉丁语，其实是英语词；下表如实区分本族要素与相关拉丁要素。

items.example: It marks the direction of the putting.
A verb of uncertain origin, recorded in Old English.
items.exampleCN: 古英语已有记录的动词，来源不确定。

items.example: It has no separate meaning now.
The partner word on the other side.
It forms inputting.
It forms inputted in some uses.
The same prefix in Latin words such as inject.
items.exampleCN: 在 inject 等拉丁词中也有同一前缀。

items.example: A Latin-rooted look-alike.

definition_en: a question asked to get information, or an official investigation into something
core_image: 一个人探身向前，皱着眉向对面的人发问
scene: 服务台的电话一直响个不停，值班员一一记录。We received several inquiries about the new course.
sceneCN: 这里 inquiry 是「询问」（第 1 个义项：为获得信息而提问）；句意为我们收到了几份关于新课程的询问。图中可辨识物件：电话、登记本、台灯。

derivatives.zh: 去掉名词后缀还原，义为「询问；调查」
同根形容词，义为「好问的；好奇的」
同根名词，义为「审问者」
由动词加表示人的后缀构成，义为「询问者」

senses.title: A question
senses.definition: a question you ask in order to get information
senses.definitionCN: 为获得信息而提出的问题
senses.example: She made an inquiry about train times.
senses.exampleCN: 她询问了火车时刻。
senses.why: In- "into" plus quaerere "to seek" gives "a seeking into": a question is a search for information.
senses.whyCN: in-「向内」加 quaerere「寻求」构成「向里寻求」：提问就是搜寻信息。

senses.title: An official investigation
senses.definition: an official process of asking questions to find out the facts about an event
senses.definitionCN: 为查明某一事件真相而进行的正式提问过程
senses.example: A public inquiry was held into the accident.
senses.exampleCN: 就那起事故举行了公开调查。
senses.why: When a whole institution asks the questions, the inquiry becomes an investigation with a verdict at the end.
senses.whyCN: 当一个机构来提问时，inquiry 就成了带结论的调查。

senses.title: Careful study of a question
senses.definition: the act of examining a subject carefully in order to understand it
senses.definitionCN: 为理解某一问题而进行的细致考察
senses.example: Scientific inquiry depends on evidence.
senses.exampleCN: 科学探究依赖证据。
senses.why: The same seeking applies to ideas: to inquire into nature is to look for its causes.
senses.whyCN: 这种「寻求」也适用于思想：探究自然是去找它的成因。

intro.en: Inquiry is a Latin compound meaning to seek into, and it covers both a polite question and a formal probe.
intro.cn: inquiry 是拉丁语意为「向里寻求」的复合词，兼指礼貌的提问与正式调查。

items.en: Quaerere meant "to seek, ask", the source of question, query and quest.
items.cn: quaerere 意为「寻求、询问」，是 question、query、quest 的来源。

items.en: Inquirere, from in- plus quaerere, meant "to seek into, investigate".
items.cn: inquirere 由 in- 加 quaerere 构成，意为「向里寻求、调查」。

items.en: Inquisitio was a legal searching out of facts, the noun behind English inquiry.
items.cn: inquisitio 是法律上对事实的追查，是英语 inquiry 背后的名词。

items.en: Old French enquerre passed the verb to English as enquire and inquire.
items.cn: 古法语 enquerre 把动词传入英语，作 enquire 与 inquire。

items.en: The noun inquiry serves both everyday questions and official investigations.
items.cn: 名词 inquiry 兼用于日常询问与正式调查。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the Latin verb of seeking; the near-meaning group gathers other words for questions and probes.
note.cn: 形近组共享拉丁语「寻求」动词；近义组收其他表示提问与调查的词。

entries.definition: The verb meaning to ask or investigate.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「询问、调查」。

entries.definition: A single sentence that seeks an answer.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「问题」，同根。

entries.definition: Eager to know and to ask, often about others.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「好问的、好奇的」。

entries.definition: A systematic official search for facts.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「调查」，强调系统、正式地查明事实。

entries.definition: A thorough enquiry, often by journalists or officials.
entries.definitionCN: 名词或动词，义为「探查」，常指记者或官员的深入追查。

entries.definition: The act of politely asking for something to be given.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「请求」，指礼貌地要求某物。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use quaerere, the Latin verb of seeking, and the phrases inquiry appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子使用拉丁语「寻求」动词 quaerere，以及 inquiry 的常用搭配。

normal.en: Quaerere is to seek: an inquiry is a search, with words as the torch.
normal.cn: quaerere 是「寻求」：inquiry 是一次搜寻，言语就是火把。

normal.en: Question and inquiry share the root: one is a single question, the other a search.
normal.cn: question 与 inquiry 同根：前者是单个问题，后者是一次查寻。

normal.en: Make an inquiry is the polite phrase; hold an inquiry is the official one.
normal.cn: make an inquiry 是礼貌说法，hold an inquiry 是官方说法。

normal.en: British spelling often writes enquiry for a simple question.
normal.cn: 英式拼写常用 enquiry 指简单询问。

normal.en: A formal inquiry into the accident lasted a year.
normal.cn: 对这起事故的正式调查持续了一年。

abstract.en: Picture a lamp held into a dark room: enquiry is light aimed at what is unknown.
abstract.cn: 想象一盏灯举进暗室：探究就是照向未知的光。

abstract.en: Every question is a small expedition into someone else's knowledge.
abstract.cn: 每个问题都是进入他人知识领域的一次小型远征。

abstract.en: Good inquiry asks without assuming, and listens without hurrying.
abstract.cn: 好的询问不预设答案，也不急着插话。

examples.en: We have had many inquiries about the job.
examples.cn: 我们收到了许多关于这份工作的询问。

examples.en: An independent inquiry was set up into the fire.
examples.cn: 就这场火灾成立了独立调查。

examples.en: Free inquiry is the basis of any science.
examples.cn: 自由探究是一切科学的基础。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「因快瑞」——因想快点知道结果，就去询问调查

root: 拉丁语 quaerere「寻求、询问」加 in-「向内」构成 inquirere「探究」，名词 inquisitio 经古法语 enquere 传入英语，作 inquire 与 inquiry；同根词有 question、query、quest、inquisitive。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses on one thread: a question, an official investigation, and the careful study of a subject.
sensesIntro.cn: 三个义项串在一条线上：一个问题、一次正式调查，以及对某一课题的细致探究。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a lamp is held into a dark room.
core.cn: 核心意象：一盏灯被举进黑暗的房间。

branches.en: THE DESK: many inquiries arrive at an office that serves the public.
branches.cn: 服务台这条线：公共机构会收到大量 inquiry。

branches.en: THE LETTER: a written inquiry asks politely and waits for a reply.
branches.cn: 信件这条线：书面 inquiry 礼貌发问，静待回复。

branches.en: THE COURT: an official inquiry gathers evidence and publishes a report.
branches.cn: 法庭这条线：正式 inquiry 收集证据并公布报告。

branches.en: THE LAB: scientific inquiry tests ideas against evidence.
branches.cn: 实验室这条线：科学探究用证据检验观念。

branches.en: THE THREAD: each sense is a structured search for what is not yet known.
branches.cn: 线索这条线：每个义项都是对未知之物的有组织搜寻。

intro.en: Inquiry is a Latin prefix on a Latin verb of seeking, with a noun ending added.
intro.cn: inquiry 由拉丁语前缀加「寻求」动词构成，再加名词词尾。

latinIntro.en: Latin quaerere, inquirere and inquisitio are recorded; the spelling with y is English.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 quaerere、inquirere、inquisitio 均有记录；带 y 的拼写是英语的变化。

items.example: It directs the seeking inward.
The root also gives question.
The compound behind the word.
items.exampleCN: 这是本词背后的复合动词。

items.example: The noun model for inquiry.
It shapes the English noun.
It forms inquisitive.
It forms inquisitor.
It forms inquirer.

definition_en: a small animal with six legs and a body in three parts, such as an ant or a bee
core_image: 一片叶子背面，一只甲虫的身体被切成头、胸、腹三段
scene: 夏夜的灯下，小飞虫不断撞在玻璃上。A tiny insect crawled across the page and stopped on a word.
sceneCN: 这里 insect 是「昆虫」（第 1 个义项：身体三节、六足的小动物）；句意为一只小虫爬过纸页，停在一个词上。图中可辨识物件：叶片、甲虫、台灯。

derivatives.zh: 由本词加表示「杀」的后缀构成，义为「杀虫剂」
由本词加表示「食」的词根构成，义为「食虫动物」
由 insectivore 加后缀构成，义为「食虫的」
由本词加 like 构成，义为「像昆虫的」

senses.title: A six-legged small animal
senses.definition: a small creature with six legs and a body divided into head, thorax and abdomen
senses.definitionCN: 有六条腿、身体分为头胸腹三部分的小生物
senses.example: Ants, bees and beetles are all insects.
senses.exampleCN: 蚂蚁、蜜蜂和甲虫都是昆虫。
senses.why: Insectum means cut into: Roman writers named the class by its visible segments.
senses.whyCN: insectum 意为「被切开的」：罗马作家按可见的分节为这一类命名。

senses.title: Any small crawling creature in loose speech
senses.definition: in everyday language, almost any small crawling or flying bug
senses.definitionCN: 在日常语言中，泛指任何小爬虫或飞虫
senses.example: Something insect-like moved in the grass.
senses.exampleCN: 有像虫子的东西在草丛里动。
senses.why: In loose use the word covers any creeping small creature, though spiders are not insects.
senses.whyCN: 在宽泛用法中它涵盖任何小爬虫，尽管蜘蛛并不属于昆虫。

intro.en: Insect is a Latin word meaning "cut into", given by ancient naturalists who saw the body in sections.
intro.cn: insect 是拉丁语「切开的」一词，古代博物学家见其身体分节而命名。

items.en: Secare meant "to cut", the source of section and segment.
items.cn: secare 意为「切」，是 section 与 segment 的来源。

items.en: Insectum, from in- "into" plus secare, meant "cut into" or "notched".
items.cn: insectum 由 in-「向内」加 secare 构成，意为「切开的、有刻痕的」。

items.en: Pliny and other Roman writers used insecta for animals whose bodies show cuts or segments.
items.cn: 普林尼等罗马作家用 insecta 指身体显出道道切痕或分节的动物。

items.en: English borrowed insect in the seventeenth century as natural history grew.
items.cn: 十七世纪博物学发展，英语借入 insect 一词。

items.en: Later science narrowed it to the six-legged class, while speech kept the looser sense.
items.cn: 后来科学把它收窄到六足纲，口语仍保留较宽的用法。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the Latin verb of cutting; the near-meaning group gathers other small creatures.
note.cn: 形近组共享拉丁语「切」动词；近义组收其他小型生物。

entries.definition: A part cut from a whole.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「部分、切面」，同根。

entries.definition: A chemical that kills insects.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「杀虫剂」，由本词构成。

entries.definition: To cut something apart in order to study it.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「解剖」，同根。

entries.definition: The everyday word for a small insect, and a computer fault.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「小虫」，日常用语，也指程序错误。

entries.definition: A kind of insect with hard wing cases.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「甲虫」，昆虫的一类。

entries.definition: An eight-legged creature, not an insect at all.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「蜘蛛」，八足，并非昆虫。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use secare, the Latin verb of cutting, and the collocations the word takes.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子使用拉丁语「切」动词 secare，以及这个词的搭配。

normal.en: Secare is to cut: an insect is a body cut into three parts.
normal.cn: secare 是「切」：insect 就是被切成三部分的身体。

normal.en: Insect, section and dissect all come from the same cutting verb.
normal.cn: insect、section、dissect 都出自同一个「切」的动词。

normal.en: An insect has six legs, a spider has eight.
normal.cn: 昆虫有六条腿，蜘蛛有八条。

normal.en: Insect repellent keeps the mosquitoes away.
normal.cn: insect repellent 用来驱蚊。

normal.en: Insecticide kills insects, and insectivores eat them.
normal.cn: insecticide 杀虫，insectivore 吃虫。

abstract.en: Picture a leaf with a beetle on it, the body lined in three clear bands.
abstract.cn: 想象一片叶子上的甲虫，身体分三道清晰的纹。

abstract.en: The name is a description: nature was classified by its visible notches.
abstract.cn: 这个名字本身就是描述：自然按可见的刻痕被分类。

abstract.en: Small as insects are, they outnumber us and pollinate most of what we eat.
abstract.cn: 昆虫虽小，数量却远超我们，还为我们大部分食物授粉。

examples.en: Insects play a vital role in pollination.
examples.cn: 昆虫在授粉中起关键作用。

examples.en: He brushed the insect off his sleeve.
examples.cn: 他把袖子上的虫子拂掉了。

examples.en: This insect lives only in dry grassland.
examples.cn: 这种昆虫只生活在干燥的草原上。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「因塞克特」——因身上「塞」满了节段，才叫昆虫

root: 拉丁语 secare「切」加 in-「向内」构成 insectum「切开的、有刻痕的」，普林尼用它指体节分明的动物；十七世纪入英语，后科学上专指六足纲。同根词有 section、dissect、segment。

sensesIntro.en: Two senses: the strict zoological class, and the loose everyday word for a small bug.
sensesIntro.cn: 两个义项：严格的动物学分类，以及口语里对小虫的泛称。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a beetle on a leaf, its body divided into three clear sections.
core.cn: 核心意象：叶上的甲虫，身体分为三节。

branches.en: THE GARDEN: insects are both pests and helpers in gardens.
branches.cn: 花园这条线：insect 在园中既是害虫也是帮手。

branches.en: THE CLASS: six legs and three body parts define the zoological insect.
branches.cn: 分类这条线：六足与三节身体定义了动物学上的昆虫。

branches.en: THE NIGHT LAMP: loose speech calls every small flying thing an insect.
branches.cn: 夜灯这条线：口语把一切小飞虫都叫 insect。

branches.en: THE PAGE: a crawling speck on a book is an insect in ordinary talk.
branches.cn: 书页这条线：书上的小爬虫在日常说法里也算昆虫。

branches.en: THE THREAD: in both senses the creature is small, many-legged and everywhere.
branches.cn: 线索这条线：两种用法里，它都小而多足，无处不在。

intro.en: Insect is a Latin past participle used as a noun, with English compounds built on it later.
intro.cn: insect 是拉丁语过去分词作名词使用，后来在英语里构成复合词。

latinIntro.en: Latin secare and insectum are recorded; the adjective insectus and noun insecta both appear in Roman writers.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 secare 与 insectum 均有记录，形容词 insectus 与名词 insecta 都见于罗马作家笔下。

items.example: It marks cutting into the body.
items.exampleCN: 它标出切入身体的动作。

items.example: The root also gives section and segment.
items.exampleCN: 这一词根还给出 section 与 segment。

items.example: It appears in dissect and section.
items.exampleCN: 它出现在 dissect 与 section 中。

items.example: The Latin source of the word.
items.exampleCN: 这是本词的拉丁语来源。

items.example: It forms insecticide.
It forms insectivore.
It forms insectivorous.
It forms insect-like.

definition_zh: 在……里面；内部；里面；内在的
definition_en: in or into the interior of something, or the interior itself
core_image: 一扇半开的门，灯光从门内的屋里漏出来
scene: 雨下得很大，屋檐下一只猫缩成一团。Stay inside until the storm passes over the hill.
sceneCN: 这里 inside 是「在里面」（第 1 个义项：处于某物的内部），句意是待在屋里，等暴风雨越过山岗。画面里能看到的物件：半开的门、灯、猫、雨帘。

derivatives.zh: 由本词加 -er 构成，义为「内部人员；知情人」
由本词加复数词尾构成，义为「五脏；内脏」
由本词加 trading 构成的复合名词，义为「内幕交易」

senses.title: In the interior
senses.definition: in the inner part of a room, box, building, or other space
senses.definitionCN: 在房间、箱子、建筑或其他空间的内部
senses.example: The keys are inside the drawer, under the papers.
senses.exampleCN: 钥匙在抽屉里，压着报纸。
senses.why: In- means within and side names a surface; inside is literally the inner side of something.
senses.whyCN: in- 意为「在内」，side 指某一面；inside 字面上就是某物的内侧。

senses.title: Towards the interior
senses.definition: moving from outdoors to the inner part of a place
senses.definitionCN: 从外面移到某地的内部
senses.example: It started to rain, so we went inside.
senses.exampleCN: 开始下雨了，于是我们走进屋里。
senses.why: The same form works without an object as an adverb: the direction inwards is inside as well.
senses.whyCN: 同一形式不带宾语时作副词：朝里的方向也是 inside。

senses.title: The inner surface
senses.definition: the part of an object that faces inwards, opposite the outer surface
senses.definitionCN: 物体朝内的一面，与外面相对
senses.example: The inside of the cup is stained brown.
senses.exampleCN: 杯子的内侧被染成了褐色。
senses.why: As a noun the word names the surface itself, so the cup has an outside and an inside.
senses.whyCN: 作名词时它指那个面本身，所以杯子有外壁也有内壁。

senses.title: Within a period or a group
senses.titleCN: 在一段时间或群体之内
senses.definition: within a stated period of time, or within a group of people
senses.definitionCN: 在某一时间段之内，或在一群人内部
senses.example: The parcel will arrive inside three days.
senses.exampleCN: 包裹将在三天之内送到。
senses.why: Time and organisations are pictured as containers, so being within them is also being inside.
senses.whyCN: 时间与组织被想象成容器，因此身处其中也就是 inside。

intro.en: Inside is a native English compound of in and side, first written as two words and later joined.
intro.cn: inside 是英语本族语复合词，由 in 与 side 组成，早期分写，后来合成一个词。

items.en: The preposition in and the noun side, both Old English, named location and surface separately.
items.cn: 介词 in 与名词 side 都见于古英语，分别表示位置与某个面。

items.en: The phrase in side "in the side or interior" appears in Middle English, often written as two words.
items.cn: 中古英语出现短语 in side「在某一面之内」，常分写作两个词。

items.en: By the sixteenth century inside is written as one word and works as preposition, adverb and noun.
items.cn: 到十六世纪，inside 已合写成一个词，可作介词、副词与名词。

items.en: The adjective use, as in inside pocket, develops in the eighteenth century.
items.cn: 形容词用法（如 inside pocket）在十八世纪发展出来。

items.en: Later phrases such as inside out and inside information extend it to metaphor.
items.cn: 后来的 inside out、inside information 又把它延伸到比喻用法。

note.en: The look-alike group is built on the same in- pattern; the near-meaning group holds other words for being within.
note.cn: 形近组按同样的 in- 构词方式展开；近义组收其他表示「在里面」的词。

entries.definition: The reverse of inside, naming the outer part or the outdoors.
entries.definitionCN: 名词/介词，义为「外面」，是 inside 的反面。

entries.definition: Next to something; shares side but not the inner meaning.
entries.definitionCN: 介词，义为「在……旁边」，与 side 有关但无「内部」义。

entries.definition: Directed towards the inside, formed with the Old English suffix -ward.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词/副词，义为「向内的」，用古英语后缀 -ward 构成。

entries.definition: Inside a place, group or period; more formal than inside.
entries.definitionCN: 介词，义为「在……之内」，比 inside 更正式。

entries.definition: Inside a building, used only as an adverb.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「在室内」，只作副词用。

entries.definition: The inner part, especially of a building or a country.
entries.definitionCN: 名词/形容词，义为「内部」，多指建筑或国家的内陆。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the two halves of the word and the phrases that fix its meaning.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子利用这个词的两半，以及固定其含义的搭配。

normal.en: in plus side: the side that is in.
normal.cn: in 加 side：朝里的那一面。

normal.en: Outside and inside are a matched pair.
normal.cn: outside 与 inside 是一对。

normal.en: Inside out describes a shirt worn wrongly.
normal.cn: inside out 形容衣服穿反了。

normal.en: Inside information comes from people who are inside a group.
normal.cn: inside information 来自身处群体内部的人。

normal.en: Take the keys inside before the rain starts.
normal.cn: 下雨前把钥匙拿进屋里。

abstract.en: Think of every building as a box with a soft inner lining.
abstract.cn: 把每座建筑想成一只带柔软内衬的盒子。

abstract.en: Being inside a group feels like standing behind a door.
abstract.cn: 身处群体内部，就像站在一扇门后面。

abstract.en: Time is a room too: three days inside is a room you walk out of.
abstract.cn: 时间也是一间屋：三天之内是一间你能走出去的屋。

examples.en: The children were playing inside because of the rain.
examples.cn: 因为下雨，孩子们在室内玩。

examples.en: There is a note inside the box.
examples.cn: 盒子里面有一张纸条。

examples.en: He knows the inside of the business.
examples.cn: 他了解这个行业的内部情况。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「硬塞的」——东西硬塞到里面去了

root: 英语本族语复合词，古英语 in「在内」+ side「面、侧」，中古英语分写作 in side，十六世纪合写为 inside，作介词、副词与名词；十八世纪起有形容词用法。

sensesIntro.en: Four senses: position inside, direction inwards, the inner surface, and being within time or a group.
sensesIntro.cn: 四个义项：在内部的位置、朝里的方向、内表面，以及处于时间或群体之内。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: light leaks from behind a half-open door towards the rainy street.
core.cn: 核心意象：光从半开的门后漏向雨中的街。

branches.en: THE ROOM: something sits in the inner space of a place.
branches.cn: 房间这条线：某物处在某地的内部空间。

branches.en: THE DOORWAY: movement from outside to in.
branches.cn: 门洞这条线：从外到里的移动。

branches.en: THE CUP: the inner surface of an object.
branches.cn: 杯子这条线：物体的内表面。

branches.en: THE CLOCK AND THE TEAM: time and groups as containers.
branches.cn: 钟表与团队这条线：时间与群体被当作容器。

branches.en: THE LINK: space and surface are two views of the same interior.
branches.cn: 连接线：空间与表面是同一内部的两个视角。

intro.en: Inside is a native compound: the Old English preposition in plus the noun side.
intro.cn: inside 是本族语复合词：古英语介词 in 加名词 side。

latinIntro.en: Neither half is Latin; the related Latin prefix in- is listed only for comparison.
latinIntro.cn: 两半都不来自拉丁语，这里列出的拉丁前缀 in- 仅供对照。

items.example: The first half marks the container.
The second half names which surface.
The exact reverse of inside.
The -er ending names a person.
The old suffix -ward means direction.
A different compound with a similar sense.
items.exampleCN: 另一个含义相近的复合词。

items.example: Formed with the old adverb suffix -s.
items.exampleCN: 由古副词词尾 -s 构成。

items.example: The Latin-based word for the same idea.

definition_en: to say firmly that something must happen or is true, and refuse to give way
core_image: 一个人双手按在桌上，把同一句话再说一遍
scene: 饭馆里两个人抢着付账，谁也不肯退让。She insisted on paying for the meal herself.
sceneCN: 这里 insist 是「坚持要求」（第 1 个义项：坚决要求某事必须如此）；句意为她坚持自己付这顿饭钱。图中可辨识物件：账单、餐桌、钱包。

pos.zh: 动词：坚持；坚决要求；坚称

collocations.zh: 如果你一定要这样的话

derivatives.zh: 由本词加名词后缀构成，义为「坚持；坚决主张」
由本词加形容词后缀构成，义为「坚持的；迫切的」
由形容词加副词后缀构成，义为「坚持地」

senses.title: To demand firmly
senses.definition: to demand something firmly, refusing to accept a refusal
senses.definitionCN: 坚决要求某事，不接受拒绝
senses.example: He insisted on seeing the manager.
senses.exampleCN: 他坚持要见经理。
senses.why: Insistere is to stand upon: a demand repeats until the ground no longer moves.
senses.whyCN: insistere 是「站上去」：要求反复提出，直到脚下的地面不再移动。

senses.title: To state firmly as true
senses.definition: to say something firmly and repeatedly as true, even when others doubt it
senses.definitionCN: 在他人怀疑时仍反复断言某事为真
senses.example: She insists that she never saw the letter.
senses.exampleCN: 她坚称自己从未见过那封信。
senses.why: A claim insisted upon is a claim the speaker will not withdraw under doubt.
senses.whyCN: 被 insist 的主张，是说话者在质疑下也不撤回的主张。

intro.en: Insist is Latin in- plus sistere "to stand": to keep standing on a point.
intro.cn: insist 是拉丁语 in- 加 sistere「站立」：坚持站在某一点上。

items.en: Sistere meant "to stand, to stop, to set in place".
items.cn: sistere 意为「站立、停住、安置」。

items.en: Insistere, from in- plus sistere, meant "to stand upon, to press upon".
items.cn: insistere 由 in- 加 sistere 构成，意为「站在上面、压在上面」。

items.en: In argument the image became to stand firm on a demand or a claim.
items.cn: 在辩论中，这一意象演变为在要求或主张上站稳脚跟。

items.en: French insister passed the verb to English in the sixteenth century.
items.cn: 法语 insister 在十六世纪把这个动词传入英语。

items.en: English insists on something, insists that something is true, or insists that someone act.
items.cn: 英语里可以说 insist on 某事、insist that 某事为真，或 insist that 某人去做。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the Latin verb of standing still; the near-meaning group gathers verbs of firm demand.
note.cn: 形近组共享拉丁语「站住」动词；近义组收表示坚决要求的动词。

entries.definition: To stand against something.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「抵抗」，即站在对面。

entries.definition: To keep standing, to continue stubbornly.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「坚持、持续」，强调一直不停。

entries.definition: To stand together, to be made up of.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「由……组成」。

entries.definition: To ask for something as a right, forcefully.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「要求」，语气强硬，带有权利意味。

entries.definition: To keep saying that something is true.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「坚持声称」，多见于书面。

entries.definition: To keep doing something despite difficulty.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「执意坚持」，强调不顾阻力的持续。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use sistere, the verb of standing, and the patterns insist appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子使用「站立」动词 sistere，以及 insist 的句型。

normal.en: Sistere is to stand: to insist is to stand on a point and not move off it.
normal.cn: sistere 是「站立」：insist 就是站在一点上不让步。

normal.en: Insist on takes an -ing form: insist on paying.
normal.cn: insist on 后接动名词：insist on paying。

normal.en: Insist that can also trigger a bare verb: they insist that he leave.
normal.cn: insist that 后也可接动词原形：they insist that he leave。

normal.en: Resist, persist and insist all involve taking a stand.
normal.cn: resist、persist、insist 都与「站定立场」有关。

normal.en: If you insist is the polite way to give way.
normal.cn: if you insist 是礼貌让步的说法。

abstract.en: Picture feet planted on one stone while the argument washes around them.
abstract.cn: 想象双脚牢牢踩在一块石上，争论在四周翻涌。

abstract.en: To insist is to make your position stronger than the pressure against it.
abstract.cn: 坚持就是让自己的位置强过压来的力量。

abstract.en: Firmness can protect another person's dignity, or simply one's own pride.
abstract.cn: 执着既能保护他人的体面，也可能只是护住自己的骄傲。

examples.en: They insisted on checking every detail.
examples.cn: 他们坚持要核对每一个细节。

examples.en: He insisted that the money was his.
examples.cn: 他坚称那笔钱是他的。

examples.en: If you insist, I will come with you.
examples.cn: 如果你一定要这样，我就陪你去。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「因塞斯特」——因他「塞」住不放，才叫坚持

root: 拉丁语 sistere「站立」加 in-「在上」构成 insistere「站上去、压上去」，在争论中引申为坚持主张；经法语 insister 于十六世纪入英语。同根词有 resist、persist、consist、exist。

sensesIntro.en: Two senses: standing firm on a demand, and standing firm on a claim of fact.
sensesIntro.cn: 两个义项：在要求上站稳立场，以及在事实主张上站稳立场。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: feet planted on a single stone while the argument swirls round.
core.cn: 核心意象：双脚踩定一块石头，争论在四周盘旋。

branches.en: THE TABLE: one diner insists on paying the whole bill.
branches.cn: 餐桌这条线：一位客人 insists on 付整笔账单。

branches.en: THE OFFICE: a customer insists on seeing a manager.
branches.cn: 办公室这条线：顾客 insist on 见经理。

branches.en: THE COURT: a witness insists that the facts were as stated.
branches.cn: 法庭这条线：证人坚称事实就是所述那样。

branches.en: THE FAMILY: people insist on being right within their own homes.
branches.cn: 家庭这条线：人在自己家里也要 insist 自己是对的。

branches.en: THE THREAD: both senses refuse to let the point be moved.
branches.cn: 线索这条线：两个义项都拒绝让那个点被挪动。

intro.en: Insist is a Latin prefix on the verb for standing, and English keeps its Latin stem.
intro.cn: insist 是拉丁语前缀加「站立」动词，英语沿用其拉丁词干。

latinIntro.en: Latin sistere, insistere and the related stare are recorded.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 sistere、insistere 以及相关的 stare 均有记录。

items.example: It marks standing upon a point.
The root of resist and persist.
items.exampleCN: resist 与 persist 的词根。

items.example: The direct source of insist.
items.exampleCN: 这是 insist 的直接来源。

items.example: It survives in all the English forms.
items.exampleCN: 它在英语各形式中留存。

items.example: It forms insistence.
It forms insistent.
It forms insistently.
The same root with re-.

definition_en: a careful look at something to judge its condition, quality, or safety
core_image: 戴手套的人俯身贴近机器，用手电照着焊缝一寸寸看过去
scene: 车间里机器刚停下，一名佩戴证件的工作人员拿着手电靠近焊缝。A careful inspection showed that the pipe had a small crack.
sceneCN: 这里 inspection 是「检查」（第 1 个义项：为判断状况、质量或安全而仔细查看），句意是仔细检查后发现管道上有一条细裂缝。画面里能看到的物件：手电、焊缝、证件。

derivatives.zh: 由拉丁词干构成的后备动词，义为「检查；视察」
由本词换后缀构成，义为「检查员；督察」
由本词加 -ive 构成，义为「检查性质的」

senses.title: A careful examination
senses.definition: an official or careful look at something in order to find faults or judge quality
senses.definitionCN: 为找出问题或判断质量而进行的正式、仔细的查看
senses.example: The car passed inspection without a single fault.
senses.exampleCN: 这辆车通过检查时没有任何故障。
senses.why: Latin specere means to look; inspection is the noun of looking into a thing closely.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 specere 意为「看」；inspection 就是凑近往里面看的那个动作的名词。

senses.title: An official visit to check
senses.definition: an official visit by an authority to check that rules are being followed
senses.definitionCN: 权力机构为核查规则是否被遵守而进行的正式到访
senses.example: The school prepares for inspection every second year.
senses.exampleCN: 这所学校每隔一年准备迎接视察。
senses.why: The look becomes institutional: someone with authority comes to see whether things are done correctly.
senses.whyCN: 这种「看」被制度化了：有权的人前来看事情是否做得对。

senses.title: The act of looking closely
senses.definition: the act of examining something closely with your own eyes, often to notice details
senses.definitionCN: 用自己的眼睛仔细查看某物，往往是为了发现细节
senses.example: On closer inspection, the painting turned out to be a copy.
senses.exampleCN: 细看之下，那幅画原来是仿作。
senses.why: The oldest and simplest sense: bending down to see what the eye misses at a distance.
senses.whyCN: 最古老、最简单的义项：俯下身去看远处看不见的东西。

intro.en: Inspection is a Latin noun of action from inspicere "to look into", built on specere "to see".
intro.cn: inspection 是拉丁语 inspicere「向里看」的行为名词，基于 specere「看」。

items.en: Specere "to look at" was one of the basic verbs of seeing in Latin.
items.cn: specere「看」是拉丁语中最基本的视觉动词之一。

items.en: In- plus specere gave inspicere, "to look into, examine".
items.cn: in- 加 specere 得到 inspicere，意为「向里看、查察」。

items.en: The noun of action inspectio named the examination itself.
items.cn: 行为名词 inspectio 指查看这件事本身。

items.en: Old French passed inspection into English in the fourteenth century.
items.cn: 古法语在十四世纪把 inspection 传入英语。

items.en: Industrial and school inspection gave the word its official, regular sense.
items.cn: 工业检查与学校视察赋予了它官方、定期的含义。

note.en: The look-alike group shares Latin spec- "look"; the near-meaning group holds other words for examining.
note.cn: 形近组共享拉丁词根 spec-「看」；近义组收其他表示「检查」的词。

entries.definition: Someone who watches, built on the same looking root.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「观众」，用同一「看」词根构成。

entries.definition: To think someone is guilty, literally "to look up from below".
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「怀疑」，字面是「从下往上看」。

entries.definition: The verb behind the noun, meaning to look into closely.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，是本词背后的动词，义为「仔细查看」。

entries.definition: A close testing look, wider and more formal.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「审查」，范围更宽、更正式。

entries.definition: A quick test that looks right or works.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「检查」，强调快速确认是否正常。

entries.definition: An official examination of financial records.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「审计」，指对财务记录的正式检查。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the root spec- "look" and the prepositions that go with the word.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子利用词根 spec-「看」以及这个词常用的介词搭配。

normal.en: spec- is to look: inspection is looking in.
normal.cn: spec- 是「看」：inspection 就是往里看。

normal.en: Spectator, suspect and inspect all share the root.
normal.cn: spectator、suspect、inspect 共享词根。

normal.en: On inspection, the engine had two loose bolts.
normal.cn: 经检查，发动机上有两颗松动的螺栓。

normal.en: A safety inspection happens before a factory reopens.
normal.cn: 工厂复工前会做安全检查。

normal.en: Close inspection often finds what a quick glance misses.
normal.cn: 细看常能发现一眼扫过所遗漏的东西。

abstract.en: Picture a beam of light moving slowly along a seam.
abstract.cn: 想象一束光沿着接缝慢慢移动。

abstract.en: An inspection is a conversation between the eye and the object.
abstract.cn: 检查是眼睛与物件之间的一场对话。

abstract.en: What survives inspection deserves trust; what avoids it does not.
abstract.cn: 经得起检查的东西值得信任，躲避检查的不值得。

examples.en: The building failed its fire inspection.
examples.cn: 这座建筑未通过消防检查。

examples.en: On inspection, the letter proved to be false.
examples.cn: 经查看，那封信原来是伪造的。

examples.en: Officials made an inspection of the harbour.
examples.cn: 官员们对港口进行了视察。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「因斯佩克」——按品牌要求一项项查看，就是检查

root: 拉丁语 specere「看」→ in- + specere = inspicere「向里看、查察」→ 行为名词 inspectio「检查」→ 古法语 → 十四世纪英语 inspection。spec-/spect- 也见于 spectacle、spectator、suspect、respect。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses: a careful examination, an official visit, and plain close looking.
sensesIntro.cn: 三个义项：仔细检查、官方视察，以及朴素的「细看」。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a gloved hand guides a torch along a weld, inch by inch.
core.cn: 核心意象：戴手套的手拿着手电沿着焊縫一寸寸照。

branches.en: THE WORKSHOP: a machine is checked for faults.
branches.cn: 车间这条线：检查机器有无故障。

branches.en: THE OFFICE: an authority visits to enforce rules.
branches.cn: 机关这条线：权力部门到访核查规则。

branches.en: THE GALLERY: a closer look changes what we think.
branches.cn: 画廊这条线：凑近细看改变了我们的判断。

branches.en: THE LINK: official and personal inspection both rest on looking closely.
branches.cn: 连接线：官方检查与个人细看都靠凑近看。

branches.en: THE SCHEDULE: the official sense is regular and predictable.
branches.cn: 日程线：官方义是定期、可预期的。

intro.en: Inspection is in- "into" plus spec- "look", with the noun ending -ion.
intro.cn: inspection 是 in-「向内」加 spec-「看」，再加名词词尾 -ion。

latinIntro.en: Latin specere, inspicere and inspectio are attested, so no reconstruction is needed for this layer.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 specere、inspicere、inspectio 均有记载，这一层无需重构。

items.example: It directs the looking inward.
The root runs through spectacles and spectator.
items.exampleCN: 这一词根贯穿 spectacles 与 spectator。

items.example: The compound is the direct source.
items.exampleCN: 这一复合动词是直接来源。

items.example: It makes an abstract noun of action.
items.exampleCN: 它构成抽象的行为名词。

items.example: Inspector names the person who checks.
The same root with a different prefix-free form.
items.exampleCN: 同一词根的无前缀形式。

items.example: Re- gives the sense of looking back.
Sub- "under" plus the same root.

definition_en: a person whose job is to examine places, goods, or work and report on them
core_image: 一个带着记录本的人站在楼梯口，正在逐项核对清单
scene: 工厂门口贴着来访须知，穿制服的人把证件挂在胸前。The inspector wrote down three faults and asked to see them fixed by Friday.
sceneCN: 这里 inspector 是「检查员」（第 1 个义项：以检查场所、货物或工作为职业的人），句意是检查员记下了三处问题，并要求周五前修好。画面里能看到的物件：记录本、清单、证件。

pos.zh: 名词：检查员；督察；巡视员

derivatives.zh: 由本词换后缀构成，义为「检查；视察」
同族动词，义为「检查；视察」
由本词加 -ate 构成，义为「检查机构；督察部门」
由本词加 -ship 构成，义为「检查员职位」

senses.title: A person who examines officially
senses.definition: someone employed to look closely at buildings, food, machines, or work and report the results
senses.definitionCN: 受雇仔细查看建筑、食品、机器或工作并上报结果的人
senses.example: A health inspector closed the kitchen for a week.
senses.exampleCN: 卫生检查员把厨房关停了一周。
senses.why: The agent ending -or turns the act of looking into the person who does it.
senses.whyCN: 施事后缀 -or 把「看」这个动作变成做这个动作的人。

senses.title: A police rank
senses.definition: a police officer of middle rank, above a sergeant in many forces
senses.definitionCN: 许多警队中位于警长之上、属中层警衔的警官
senses.example: Inspector Brown took charge of the case.
senses.exampleCN: 布朗警督负责此案。
senses.why: Looking into crimes became an office with a name; the one who investigates is the inspector.
senses.whyCN: 「查察案件」变成了一种职务，负责查案的人就称为 inspector。

senses.title: A supervisor of schools or services
senses.definition: an official who visits schools or public services to check their standards
senses.definitionCN: 到访学校或公共服务机构检查其水平的官员
senses.example: The inspector sat at the back and said nothing.
senses.exampleCN: 督学坐在后排，一言不发。
senses.why: The word spread from factories to schools and railways, wherever standards had to be watched.
senses.whyCN: 这个词从工厂传到学校与铁路，凡是需要监督标准的地方都有它。

intro.en: Inspector is the Latin agent noun from inspicere "to look into", meaning literally "the one who looks in".
intro.cn: inspector 是拉丁语 inspicere「向里看」的施事名词，字面就是「往里看的人」。

items.en: Specere "to look" and the compound inspicere "to examine" are both classical.
items.cn: specere「看」与复合词 inspicere「查察」都是古典拉丁语词汇。

items.en: The agent suffix -or marked the person performing the action.
items.cn: 施事后缀 -or 标出执行动作的人。

items.en: Late Latin used inspector for an overseer or examiner.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁语用 inspector 指监工或查察者。

items.en: Old French inspecteur passed the word to English in the seventeenth century.
items.cn: 古法语 inspecteur 在十七世纪把这个词传给英语。

items.en: Railways, factories and police forces each created their own inspectors.
items.cn: 铁路、工厂与警队各自设立了自己的 inspector 职位。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the spec- root and the -or agent pattern; the near-meaning group holds other watching jobs.
note.cn: 形近组共享 spec- 词根与 -or 施事模式；近义组收其他「查看类」职业名词。

entries.definition: The verb that names the action the inspector performs.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，即 inspector 所执行的动作。

entries.definition: The act or occasion of looking into something.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「检查、视察」。

entries.definition: A watcher with no duty to report anything.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「观众」，只观看而无报告之责。

entries.definition: Someone who checks accounts rather than buildings.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「审计员」，查的是账目而不是建筑。

entries.definition: Someone who watches over staff day by day.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「主管」，日常监管员工。

entries.definition: A specialist who measures and inspects buildings or land.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「测量员、鉴定人」，专查建筑或土地。

normalIntro.en: These hooks connect the -or ending with the job and recall the real official titles.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子把 -or 词尾与职业联系起来，并复习真实的官衔。

normal.en: Inspect plus -or: the one who looks in.
normal.cn: inspect 加 -or：往里看的那个人。

normal.en: An inspector writes down what others walked past.
normal.cn: 检查员记下别人走过时忽略的东西。

normal.en: Health, fire and school all have inspectors.
normal.cn: 卫生、消防、学校都设有检查员。

normal.en: Inspector is also a police rank in Britain.
normal.cn: inspector 在英国也是警衔。

normal.en: The inspectorate is the whole office of inspectors.
normal.cn: inspectorate 指检查员组成的整个机构。

abstract.en: Picture a clipboard with legs walking the corridor.
abstract.cn: 想象一块带腿的板夹走在走廊里。

abstract.en: The inspector stands where the rules meet the real world.
abstract.cn: 检查员站在规则与现实的交界处。

abstract.en: To be inspected is to be seen as you really are.
abstract.cn: 被检查就是被如实看见。

examples.en: The inspector found broken tiles on the roof.
examples.cn: 检查员发现屋顶有破损的瓦片。

examples.en: An inspector will visit the kitchen next week.
examples.cn: 检查员下周会来厨房查看。

examples.en: She was promoted to inspector after ten years.
examples.cn: 十年后她晋升为警督。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「因斯派克特」——专门派来查看的人，就是检查员

root: 拉丁语 specere「看」→ inspicere「查察」→ 施事后缀 -or 构成晚期拉丁语 inspector「监工、查察者」→ 古法语 inspecteur → 十七世纪英语 inspector。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses: the official examiner, the police rank, and the school or service supervisor.
sensesIntro.cn: 三个义项：官方检查员、警督，以及督学类督导。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a person with a notebook stands at the foot of the stairs, ticking off a list.
core.cn: 核心意象：拿着记录本的人站在楼梯口，逐项打勾。

branches.en: THE FACTORY: the examiner of goods, food and machines.
branches.cn: 工厂这条线：检查货物、食品与机器的人。

branches.en: THE STATION: a police rank built on investigation.
branches.cn: 警局这条线：由「查案」发展出的警衔。

branches.en: THE CLASSROOM: the visiting supervisor of schools.
branches.cn: 教室这条线：到访学校的督学。

branches.en: THE LINK: all three share the duty of looking and reporting.
branches.cn: 连接线：三者都负有查看并上报之责。

branches.en: THE TONE: as a job title the word is neutral and official.
branches.cn: 语气线：作为职务名称，这个词中性而正式。

intro.en: Inspector is the stem inspect- plus the Latin agent ending -or "one who".
intro.cn: inspector 是词干 inspect- 加拉丁施事词尾 -or「做……的人」。

latinIntro.en: Latin inspicere and inspector are recorded; the agent suffix -or is regular.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 inspicere 与 inspector 均有记载，施事后缀 -or 是规则词尾。

items.example: The prefix marks the inward look.
The root also gives spectator.
It turns the action into a person.
The noun names what the inspector does.
items.exampleCN: 名词指 inspector 所做的事。

items.example: The suffix -ate marks a collective body.
A near-by job title from the same idea.
Another checker with a narrower field.
items.exampleCN: 另一位检查者，范围更窄。

items.example: Buildings instead of products.
items.exampleCN: 检查的是建筑而非产品。

definition_en: to put equipment or software in place ready for use, or to put someone formally into an office
core_image: 两个人在墙上量好位置，把一台新机器固定牢，插上电
scene: 梯子靠在墙边，工具箱摊开在地板上。The engineers will install the new heating system before winter.
sceneCN: 这里 install 是「安装」（第 1 个义项：把设备或软件安置好以便使用），句意是工程师会在入冬前安装新的供暖系统。画面里能看到的物件：梯子、工具箱、机器、电线。

pos.zh: 动词：安装；设置；正式任命

derivatives.zh: 由本词加 -ation 构成，义为「安装；装置」
由本词加 -er 构成，义为「安装者；安装程序」
由本词与 art 构成的复合名词，义为「装置艺术」

senses.title: To put equipment in place
senses.definition: to fix a machine, device, or piece of equipment in position and connect it so that it works
senses.definitionCN: 把机器、装置或设备固定在位置上并接好线，使其能工作
senses.example: They installed a shower in the small bathroom.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在小浴室里装了淋浴。
senses.why: Latin in- "in" plus stallum "a place, a stall": to install is to set something in its proper place.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 in-「入」加 stallum「位置、座位」：install 就是把东西放到它该在的位置上。

senses.title: To set up software
senses.definition: to copy a program onto a computer or phone and prepare it to run
senses.definitionCN: 把程序复制到电脑或手机上并准备好运行
senses.example: It took ten minutes to install the app.
senses.exampleCN: 装这个应用花了十分钟。
senses.why: The medieval seat became a digital one: the program is put into place inside the machine.
senses.whyCN: 中世纪的「座位」变成了数字的：程序被放进机器的位置里。

senses.title: To put someone into an office
senses.definition: to place a person formally in an official position, often with a ceremony
senses.definitionCN: 以仪式等方式正式把某人安置到官职上
senses.example: The new bishop was installed in the cathedral in spring.
senses.exampleCN: 新主教春天在大教堂正式就职。
senses.why: The oldest sense: a person is seated in a stall, the literal seat of office.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的义项：人坐进 stallum（座位），即「入座就职」。

intro.en: Install comes from medieval Latin installare "to place in a stall or seat", a church word first.
intro.cn: install 来自中世纪拉丁语 installare「安置到座位里」，最初是教会用语。

items.en: Stallum meant a standing place, a stall, or a seat in a choir.
items.cn: stallum 指站立之处、摊位，或唱诗班的座位。

items.en: Installare "to put into a stall" was used of clergy placed in a prebend or a canonry.
items.cn: installare「放入座位」用于指把教士安置到俸禄或教会职位上。

items.en: Old French installer carried the word into secular use for any placing in office.
items.cn: 古法语 installer 使这个词进入世俗用法，泛指就职。

items.en: English borrowed the verb with the sense "to place" from the fifteenth century, first for church appointments.
items.cn: 英语从十五世纪起用其「安放」之义，最初用于教会任命。

items.en: Industrial and computing usage later extended it to machines and software.
items.cn: 后来的工业与计算机用法又把它扩展到机器与软件。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the -stall place word; the near-meaning group holds other verbs of putting things in place.
note.cn: 形近组共享 -stall「位置」这一部分；近义组收其他表示「放置」的动词。

entries.definition: A booth or a stable compartment, the literal place of the root.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「摊位、隔间」，是词根字面的「位置」。

entries.definition: The act of installing, or the equipment installed.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「安装」或「装好的装置」。

entries.definition: A person or program that installs something.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「安装者」或「安装程序」。

entries.definition: To put a part in place and make it work, common in British speech.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「装配」，英式口语常用。

entries.definition: To prepare equipment for use, often on a temporary basis.
entries.definitionCN: 动词短语，义为「设置」，常指临时搭建。

entries.definition: To fix something firmly onto a surface or frame.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「镶嵌、安装」，强调牢固固定在表面。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the literal "seat" inside the word and the objects people install.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子利用词内字面的「座位」，以及人们真实安装的东西。

normal.en: in plus stall: put the thing into its stall.
normal.cn: in 加 stall：把东西放进它的位置。

normal.en: Stall is still a booth; install is seating a machine.
normal.cn: stall 仍是摊位；install 是让机器落座。

normal.en: Install software, then install the printer.
normal.cn: 先装软件，再装打印机。

normal.en: A bishop is installed in a cathedral seat.
normal.cn: 主教的就职是在教堂的座位上完成的。

normal.en: Two l is correct: installed, not installd.
normal.cn: 过去式要双写 l：installed。

abstract.en: Every installation is a promise that the thing will stay put.
abstract.cn: 每一次安装都是一份「它会留着不动」的承诺。

abstract.en: A new habit must be installed like a new boiler.
abstract.cn: 新习惯要像新锅炉一样被装进去。

abstract.en: Installing is a small ceremony of order.
abstract.cn: 安装是一场微小的秩序仪式。

examples.en: We installed new locks on every door.
examples.cn: 我们在每扇门上都装了新锁。

examples.en: The software installs itself in a few minutes.
examples.cn: 这个软件几分钟就自动装好了。

examples.en: He was installed as head of the department last year.
examples.cn: 他去年正式就任部门负责人。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「硬装」——硬要装进去，就是安装

root: 中世纪拉丁语 stallum「站立处、摊位、座位」→ installare「放入座位」→ 古法语 installer → 十五世纪英语。最早用于教会就职，后转指机器与软件的安装。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses: fixing equipment, copying software, and seating a person in office.
sensesIntro.cn: 三个义项：固定设备、装软件，以及让人正式就职。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two workers measure the wall and bolt a new machine firmly in place.
core.cn: 核心意象：两个工人量好墙面，把新机器牢牢固定住。

branches.en: THE WALL: a boiler or camera is fixed and connected.
branches.cn: 墙面这条线：锅炉或摄像头被固定并接线。

branches.en: THE SCREEN: a program is put in its place inside the machine.
branches.cn: 屏幕这条线：程序被放进机器的位置里。

branches.en: THE CATHEDRAL: a person is seated in the stall of office.
branches.cn: 教堂这条线：人被安置到官职的座位上。

branches.en: THE LINK: physical and digital installation share the idea of a proper place.
branches.cn: 连接线：实体与数字安装共享「恰当位置」的观念。

branches.en: THE ROOT: the office sense is the oldest, and the others are echoes of it.
branches.cn: 根源线：就职义最古老，其余义项是它的回声。

intro.en: Install is in- "into" plus the medieval Latin stallum "a place, stall", as a verb installare.
intro.cn: install 是 in-「入」加中世纪拉丁语 stallum「位置、摊位」构成的动词 installare。

latinIntro.en: Stallum and installare are recorded in medieval Latin; the deeper Germanic origin of stallum is not Latin.
latinIntro.cn: stallum 与 installare 有中世纪拉丁语记载，但 stallum 更深的日耳曼来源不属于拉丁语。

items.example: It marks putting into a place.
The noun supplies the destination.
The verb is the direct source.
Installation names the act.
Installer names the person or program.
The bare noun survives in English.
items.exampleCN: 不带前缀的名词仍在英语中使用。

items.example: A different word from the same family.
British usage sometimes drops one l.
items.exampleCN: 英式有时只写一个 l。

definition_en: a single case or example of something that can be used as evidence
core_image: 一叠相同的文件里，有人抽出其中一张举给你看
scene: 讨论课上大家说法各不一样，老师抬手示意安静。There are several instances of this error in the report.
sceneCN: 这里 instance 是「例子、实例」（第 1 个义项：可作证据的单个例子），句意是报告里有好几处这样的错误。画面里能看到的物件：一叠文件、被抽出的一张纸。

derivatives.zh: 同根词，义为「瞬间」，与 instance 同出「站在近前」之义
由本词加 -iate 构成，义为「实例化；举例说明」
由本词加 -ing 构成，义为「举例；实例化」，多用于计算机语境

senses.title: A single example
senses.definition: one example of something, used to show that a general statement is true
senses.definitionCN: 某一事物的一个例子，用来证明一个概括性说法成立
senses.example: This is a clear instance of poor planning.
senses.exampleCN: 这是计划不周的一个明显例子。
senses.why: Latin instare means to stand upon or press near; an instance is a case that stands right in front of you.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 instare 意为「立于其上、靠近」，instance 就是站在你眼前的那个事例。

senses.title: A particular case or occasion
senses.definition: the particular case being discussed, as opposed to cases in general
senses.definitionCN: 正在讨论的那个具体情况，与一般情况相对
senses.example: In this instance the rules do not apply.
senses.exampleCN: 在这种情况下，这些规则并不适用。
senses.why: From an example that stands out, the word widened to mean the case at hand.
senses.whyCN: 从「突出的那个例子」扩大为「眼下的这种情况」。

senses.title: In the phrase for instance
senses.definition: used in the fixed phrase for instance to introduce an example in speech
senses.definitionCN: 用于固定短语 for instance，在谈话中引出例子
senses.example: Take a tool, for instance a hammer, and describe how it is used.
senses.exampleCN: 拿一个工具，比如锤子，说明它怎么用。
senses.why: The example sense hardened into the everyday discourse phrase for instance, which shortens for example.
senses.whyCN: 「例子」义固化为日常话语短语 for instance，相当于 for example。

intro.en: Instance comes from Latin instantia "a standing near, urgency", from the verb instare "to stand upon".
intro.cn: instance 来自拉丁语 instantia「立在近前、紧迫」，出自动词 instare「立于其上」。

items.en: Stare "to stand" is one of the basic Latin verbs of position.
items.cn: stare「站立」是拉丁语中最基本的方位动词之一。

items.en: In- plus stare gave instare, "to stand upon, press upon, insist".
items.cn: in- 加 stare 得到 instare，意为「立于其上、逼近、坚持」。

items.en: The noun instantia meant urgency and insistence, and later a present case.
items.cn: 名词 instantia 指紧迫与坚持，后来指当下的具体事例。

items.en: Old French instance brought the word into English in the fourteenth century.
items.cn: 古法语 instance 在十四世纪把这个词带入英语。

items.en: The example sense becomes dominant, giving the fixed phrase for instance.
items.cn: 「例子」义取得主导，形成固定短语 for instance。

note.en: The look-alike group shares Latin stare "stand"; the near-meaning group holds other words for an example or a case.
note.cn: 形近组共享拉丁词根 stare「站立」；近义组收其他表示「例子、情况」的词。

entries.definition: A moment so pressing it stands right now.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「瞬间」，指紧迫得就在眼前的一刻。

entries.definition: Standing firm and unchanging, with con- meaning together.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「恒定的」，前缀 con- 表「一起」。

entries.definition: Standing apart, with dis- meaning away.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「距离」，前缀 dis- 表「分开」。

entries.definition: The plainest word for a thing that shows a rule.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「例子」，最朴素的同义词。

entries.definition: A particular situation, common in legal and medical use.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「案例、病例」，多用于法律与医学。

entries.definition: An event that happens, with more stress on frequency.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「发生的事件」，更强调频率。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the standing root and the fixed phrases the word lives in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子利用「站立」词根，以及这个词所处的固定短语。

normal.en: stare is to stand: an instance stands in front of you as proof.
normal.cn: stare 是「站」：instance 站在你面前作证。

normal.en: For instance is the daily way of saying for example.
normal.cn: for instance 就是日常说法的 for example。

normal.en: In this instance means in this particular case.
normal.cn: in this instance 意为「在这一具体情况中」。

normal.en: Same root as instant, constant and distance.
normal.cn: 与 instant、constant、distance 同根。

normal.en: Give one instance rather than ten adjectives.
normal.cn: 给一个实例，胜过十个形容词。

abstract.en: Picture one sheet pulled out of a stack and held up.
abstract.cn: 想象从一叠纸里抽出一张举起来。

abstract.en: An instance is a rule made visible once.
abstract.cn: 实例就是规则显形一次。

abstract.en: Arguments persuade by instances, not by volume.
abstract.cn: 论点靠实例说服人，而不是靠音量。

examples.en: There have been two instances of theft this month.
examples.cn: 本月发生了两起盗窃事件。

examples.en: In this instance, I think she is right.
examples.cn: 在这种情况下，我认为她是对的。

examples.en: For instance, a bicycle needs very little fuel.
examples.cn: 例如，自行车几乎不需要燃料。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「因此谈」——因为要谈事，所以先举一个例子

root: 拉丁语 stare「站立」→ in- + stare = instare「立于其上、逼近」→ 名词 instantia「紧迫、坚持、当下事例」→ 古法语 instance → 十四世纪英语。st-/sta- 也见于 instant、constant、distance、station。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses: one example as proof, the case at hand, and the fixed phrase for instance.
sensesIntro.cn: 三个义项：作为证据的单个例子、眼前的具体情况，以及固定短语 for instance。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one sheet is drawn from a stack and held up for everyone to see.
core.cn: 核心意象：从一叠纸里抽出一张，举给所有人看。

branches.en: THE SHEET: a single case held up as evidence.
branches.cn: 纸张这条线：举起来作证的单个事例。

branches.en: THE ROOM: the case now under discussion.
branches.cn: 房间这条线：眼下正在讨论的情况。

branches.en: THE TURN OF SPEECH: for instance introduces examples in talk.
branches.cn: 话头这条线：for instance 在谈话中引出例子。

branches.en: THE LINK: example and current case both stand in front of the speaker.
branches.cn: 连接线：例子与当下情况都站在说话者面前。

branches.en: THE HABIT: the phrase is so common that it acts like a single word.
branches.cn: 习惯线：这个短语太常用，几乎像一个词。

intro.en: Instance is in- "upon" plus the Latin standing root sta-, with the noun ending -ance.
intro.cn: instance 是 in-「在其上」加拉丁「站立」词根 sta-，再带名词词尾 -ance。

latinIntro.en: Latin stare, instare and instantia are all attested in classical texts.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 stare、instare、instantia 在古典文献中均有记载。

items.example: It marks standing close to something.
The root runs through station and stable.
items.exampleCN: 这一词根贯穿 station 与 stable。

items.example: The verb supplies the pressure of the image.
It makes a noun of state.
A close relative from the same verb.
Con- plus the same root.
Dis- means apart.
The verb form appears in technical writing.
items.exampleCN: 动词形式多见技术文献。

definition_zh: 瞬间；片刻；立即的；即食的
definition_en: an extremely short moment, or something that happens or is ready at once
core_image: 快门按下的一瞬，飞溅的水珠停在半空中
scene: 厨房里水壶刚响，桌上的杯子还在晃。The kettle boiled and the room went silent for an instant.
sceneCN: 这里 instant 是「一瞬」（第 1 个义项：极短的一刻），句意是水壶烧开，屋子里静了一瞬。画面里能看到的物件：水壶、杯子、水汽。

derivatives.zh: 由本词加 -ly 构成，义为「立即」
由本词加拉丁词尾构成，义为「瞬间发生的」
同根词，义为「例子；情况」
由本词加 -y 构成，义为「紧迫；立即」

senses.title: A very short moment
senses.definition: an extremely short period of time, too short to measure
senses.definitionCN: 极短的一段时间，短到无法计量
senses.example: For an instant she thought the room was empty.
senses.exampleCN: 有一刹那她以为屋里没人。
senses.why: Latin instans means standing upon, pressing at this very moment; an instant is the point that presses on you now.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 instans 意为「立于其上、就在此刻逼近」，instant 就是压到你眼前的那个点。

senses.title: Happening at once
senses.definition: happening or produced immediately, without delay
senses.definitionCN: 立即发生或产生的，没有延迟
senses.example: The film was an instant success with young viewers.
senses.exampleCN: 这部电影在年轻观众中一举成功。
senses.why: The pressing moment becomes a quality: what happens in that moment is instant.
senses.whyCN: 「紧迫的时刻」变成一种性质：发生在那刻的事就是 instant。

senses.title: Ready with almost no preparation
senses.definition: food or drink that is ready in seconds, needing only water
senses.definitionCN: 只需加水几秒即可食用的食品或饮料
senses.example: He keeps a jar of instant coffee in the drawer.
senses.exampleCN: 他抽屉里常放一罐速溶咖啡。
senses.why: Modern packaging applied the adjective to goods made to be ready in an instant.
senses.whyCN: 现代包装把这个形容词用于「一瞬即可备好」的商品。

intro.en: Instant is the Latin present participle of instare "to stand upon, press near", so it means "pressing on now".
intro.cn: instant 是拉丁语 instare「立于其上、逼近」的现在分词，意为「此刻正逼近的」。

items.en: Stare "to stand" is the base of a large family of position verbs.
items.cn: stare「站立」是一大群方位动词的根基。

items.en: Instare meant to stand upon, to be imminent, or to urge.
items.cn: instare 意为「立于其上、即将发生、催促」。

items.en: The participle instans "present, pressing" came to mean the present time.
items.cn: 分词 instans「当下的、紧迫的」后来被用来指「现在」。

items.en: Old French instant brought both noun and adjective into English.
items.cn: 古法语 instant 把名词与形容词一起带入英语。

items.en: Nineteenth and twentieth-century trade made instant a label for ready-made goods.
items.cn: 十九、二十世纪的商业让 instant 成为现成商品的标签。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the standing root; the near-meaning group holds other words for a very short time.
note.cn: 形近组共享「站立」词根；近义组收其他表示「极短时间」的词。

entries.definition: Standing together without change.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「恒定的」，字面是「站在一起」。

entries.definition: What stands under a thing, hence its matter.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「物质」，字面是「站在下面的东西」。

entries.definition: Something standing in the way, with ob- against.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「障碍」，前缀 ob- 表「对着、挡住」。

entries.definition: A short point in time, slightly longer than an instant.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「片刻」，比 instant 稍长。

entries.definition: A measured unit of time, more exact.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「秒」，是精确的计量单位。

entries.definition: A sudden burst of light used figuratively for a very short time.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「闪光」，比喻极短的时间。

normalIntro.en: These hooks contrast instant with instance and keep the "pressing now" image.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子对比 instant 与 instance，并保留「此刻逼近」的意象。

normal.en: Instant has a t: a point of time; instance has a c: an example.
normal.cn: instant 带 t 是时间点；instance 带 c 是例子。

normal.en: The same participle once meant the present time.
normal.cn: 这个分词曾用来指「现在」。

normal.en: In an instant is the commonest phrase in this sense.
normal.cn: in an instant 是这一义项最常见的搭配。

normal.en: Instant coffee is coffee minus the waiting.
normal.cn: 速溶咖啡就是省去等待的咖啡。

normal.en: Instant success is rare and usually luckier than it looks.
normal.cn: 一举成名很少见，通常比看上去更靠运气。

abstract.en: Picture a drop of water frozen in mid-air.
abstract.cn: 想象一滴水停在半空中。

abstract.en: An instant is the smallest room a decision can fit in.
abstract.cn: 瞬间是一个决定能容身的最小空间。

abstract.en: Every history is made of instants stacked like coins.
abstract.cn: 一切历史都由像硬币般叠起的瞬间构成。

examples.en: The room went dark for an instant.
examples.cn: 屋里黑了一瞬。

examples.en: She recognized him in an instant.
examples.cn: 她一眼就认出了他。

examples.en: Instant noodles are popular with students.
examples.cn: 方便面在学生中很受欢迎。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「因此谈的」——因此一谈就见分晓，就是一瞬间

root: 拉丁语 stare「站立」→ instare「立于其上、逼近」→ 现在分词 instans「当下的、紧迫的」→ 古法语 instant → 英语 instant，兼作名词「瞬间」与形容词「立即的」。与 instance、constant、distance 同根。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses: a point of time, immediacy as a quality, and goods ready in seconds.
sensesIntro.cn: 三个义项：一个时间点、作为性质的「立即」，以及几秒即成的商品。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a water drop hangs frozen in the air after the shutter clicks.
core.cn: 核心意象：快门按下后，水珠凝在半空中。

branches.en: THE SHUTTER: a time too short to measure.
branches.cn: 快门这条线：短到无法计量的时间。

branches.en: THE APPLAUSE: success that comes at once.
branches.cn: 掌声这条线：立刻到来的成功。

branches.en: THE JAR: goods ready without waiting.
branches.cn: 罐子这条线：无需等待即成的商品。

branches.en: THE LINK: the moment and the quality share the idea of no delay.
branches.cn: 连接线：时间点与性质共享「没有延迟」。

branches.en: THE LABEL: trade made the adjective a packaging word.
branches.cn: 标签线：商业把它变成了包装用语。

intro.en: Instant is in- plus the Latin participle stem sta-nt-, literally "standing upon".
intro.cn: instant 是 in- 加拉丁分词词干 sta-nt-，字面是「立在其上的」。

latinIntro.en: Latin instare and the participle instans are both classical and well attested.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 instare 与分词 instans 都是古典且有充分记载的形式。

items.example: It marks standing right upon the moment.
items.exampleCN: 它标出「正压在这一刻上」。

items.example: The root is visible in station and stable.
items.exampleCN: 这一词根见于 station 与 stable。

items.example: It keeps the word a participle in form.
items.exampleCN: 它让这个词在形式上保持分词。

items.example: The suffix -ly makes the adverb.
A longer adjective in technical use.
items.exampleCN: 技术语域中较长的形容词。

items.example: Con- gives the idea of together.
Sub- means under.
The root appears without a prefix.
items.exampleCN: 这一词根的无前缀形式。

definition_en: in place of something else, or as an alternative to what was expected
core_image: 两把椅子中间空出一个位子，一个人绕过去坐到了另一边
scene: 菜单上原先想点的鱼已经卖完了，服务员指了另一道菜。The fish was gone, so we had soup instead.
sceneCN: 这里 instead 是「代替、作为替代」（第 1 个义项：取代原定的那样东西），句意是鱼卖完了，所以我们改喝汤。画面里可想象的物件：菜单、空盘子、另一道菜。

pos.zh: 副词：代替；反而；作为替代

derivatives.zh: 由本词加 of 构成的短语介词，义为「而不是」
由本词去掉前缀构成的名词，义为「位置；替代」
同族词，义为「坚定的」，由 stead 与 fast 组成

senses.title: In place of another thing
senses.definition: used when one thing replaces another that was planned, expected, or available
senses.definitionCN: 当一样东西取代原本计划、预期或已有的另一样时使用
senses.example: We walked instead of taking the bus.
senses.exampleCN: 我们没坐公交，而是走了过去。
senses.why: in plus stead, an old noun for place: instead is literally "in the place of".
senses.whyCN: in 加 stead（古语中指「位置」的名词）：instead 字面上就是「在……的位置上」。

senses.title: As a contrast to what was expected
senses.definition: used to introduce something that is the reverse of what was expected
senses.definitionCN: 用来引出与预期相反的事
senses.example: The medicine did not help; instead it made him sleepy.
senses.exampleCN: 这药没起作用，反而让他犯困。
senses.why: When the substitute is unexpected, "in its place" turns into "on the contrary".
senses.whyCN: 当替代者出乎意料时，「在其位置」就转为「相反」。

senses.title: As a better alternative
senses.definition: used when suggesting a different and usually better course of action
senses.definitionCN: 在建议另一条通常更好的做法时使用
senses.example: Try the small shop instead; it is cheaper.
senses.exampleCN: 不如去那家小店，更便宜。
senses.why: Advice often offers a place to stand in another place: the word marks the swap.
senses.whyCN: 建议常常是「换上另一个位置」：这个词标出这种替换。

intro.en: Instead is a native English phrase, in plus the old noun stead "place", which had already merged into one word by the Middle Ages.
intro.cn: instead 是本族英语短语 in 加古名词 stead「位置」，中古英语时已合成一个词。

items.en: Stede meant a place, a position, or a standing spot.
items.cn: stede 意为「位置、地方、站立之处」。

items.en: The phrase in stede "in place of" is common in Middle English and often written as two words.
items.cn: 中古英语常见 in stede「代替」这一短语，常分写。

items.en: Instead of, with of added, appears by the fourteenth century and becomes a fixed preposition.
items.cn: 十四世纪出现加 of 的 instead of，并固定为短语介词。

items.en: By the sixteenth century instead stands alone as an adverb at the start of a clause.
items.cn: 十六世纪起 instead 可单独作副词出现在句首。

items.en: The "on the contrary" sense develops alongside, from sentences that name a surprise.
items.cn: 「反而」义随之发展，来自引出入意料之事的分句。

note.en: The look-alike group is built on stead "place"; the near-meaning group holds other words of substitution.
note.cn: 形近组建立在 stead「位置」之上；近义组收其他表示「替代」的词。

entries.definition: The old noun for place that survives in compounds.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「位置」，只保留在复合词中。

entries.definition: Firm in place, from the same root for standing.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「稳固的」，词根同是「位置」。

entries.definition: A house and its land, literally "home place".
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「农庄」，字面是「家的地方」。

entries.definition: Preferably, or on the contrary, depending on the sentence.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「宁可」或「相反」，取决于句意。

entries.definition: Introducing another option, more formal than instead.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「或者」，比 instead 更正式。

entries.definition: The full prepositional phrase behind the word's meaning.
entries.definitionCN: 短语介词，义为「代替」，即这个词字面的意思。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the "place" sense of stead and the difference between instead and instead of.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子利用 stead 的「位置」义，以及 instead 与 instead of 的区别。

normal.en: in plus stead, place: instead is standing in the place of another.
normal.cn: in 加 stead（位置）：instead 就是站在另一物的位置上。

normal.en: Stead survives in steady and homestead.
normal.cn: stead 还留在 steady 与 homestead 里。

normal.en: Instead takes no object; instead of needs one.
normal.cn: instead 不带宾语；instead of 必须带宾语。

normal.en: We walked instead of waiting for a bus.
normal.cn: 我们没等公交，而是走路去。

normal.en: Instead often starts a sentence with a comma.
normal.cn: instead 常置于句首并跟逗号。

abstract.en: Picture an empty chair that someone else sits down in.
abstract.cn: 想象一张空椅子被另一个人坐了下去。

abstract.en: Instead is the mark of a plan that changed.
abstract.cn: instead 是计划改变的标记。

abstract.en: Choosing instead is still choosing.
abstract.cn: 改选另一个，也仍然是选择。

examples.en: I could not sleep, so I read instead.
examples.cn: 我睡不着，于是改看书。

examples.en: She drank water instead of coffee this morning.
examples.cn: 今早她喝水而不是咖啡。

examples.en: The rain stopped; instead, the wind grew worse.
examples.cn: 雨停了，可风反而更大了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「因死呆的」——因为原计划死呆了，只好换一个

root: 古英语 stede「位置、地方」→ 中古英语短语 in stede「在……的位置上」→ instead（合写）→ 十四世纪起加 of 构成 instead of。stead 也见于 steady、homestead。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses: replacing a thing, contrasting with expectation, and offering a better option.
sensesIntro.cn: 三个义项：替换某物、与预期相反，以及提出更好的选择。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an empty chair is taken by somebody else while the expected guest is late.
core.cn: 核心意象：空椅子被另一个人坐了，预期的人却还没来。

branches.en: THE CHAIR: one thing takes the place of another.
branches.cn: 椅子这条线：一样东西占了另一样的位置。

branches.en: THE SURPRISE: the substitute is the opposite of what was hoped.
branches.cn: 意外这条线：替代者与期望正相反。

branches.en: THE ADVICE: a better option is offered in place of the first.
branches.cn: 建议这条线：用更好的选择代替原来的。

branches.en: THE LINK: both are swaps, one neutral, one recommended.
branches.cn: 连接线：两者都是替换，一个中性，一个带推荐。

branches.en: THE TONE: the contrast sense is the most emphatic.
branches.cn: 语气线：「反而」义语气最强。

intro.en: Instead is in plus the Old English noun stede "place"; it is a native compound, not a Latin one.
intro.cn: instead 是 in 加古英语名词 stede「位置」，属本族语复合词，不是拉丁来源。

latinIntro.en: No Latin root is involved; the Latin loco "in place of" is listed only as a comparison.
latinIntro.cn: 这里不涉及拉丁词根，列出的拉丁语 loco「代替」仅供对照。

items.example: The first half marks the position.
The second half supplies the place.
The prepositional form takes an object.
The bare noun survives in a few compounds.
items.exampleCN: 不带前缀的名词留存在少数复合词中。

items.example: The root is still visible.
Compound of home and stead.
items.exampleCN: 由 home 与 stead 复合。

items.example: A close synonym in advice sentences.
items.exampleCN: 在建议句中与 instead 近义。

items.example: A formal synonym for the choice sense.

definition_en: an organisation set up for research or teaching, or to set such a thing up
core_image: 几个人在空地上立起一块牌子，牌子围出一块新划定的地方
scene: 街角老楼前挂上了一块新铜牌，门厅里刚摆好桌椅。The city decided to institute a new system for waste collection.
sceneCN: 这里 institute 是动词「设立、建立」（第 2 个义项：把制度或机构建立起来），句意是市政府决定设立新的垃圾收集制度。画面里能看到的物件：铜牌、桌椅、牌子。

derivatives.zh: 由本词加 -ion 构成，义为「机构；制度」
由 institution 加 -al 构成，义为「机构的；制度性的」
由过去分词转作形容词，义为「已设立的」

senses.title: To set up a rule or system
senses.definition: to start a new rule, system, or practice and put it into effect
senses.definitionCN: 开始实行新的规则、制度或做法
senses.example: The council instituted a fine for late payment.
senses.exampleCN: 市议会设立了逾期缴费罚款。
senses.why: Latin instituere means to set up; a rule is set up much as a building is.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 instituere 意为「设立」；规则被设立起来，就像建筑被立起来一样。

senses.title: An organisation for research
senses.definition: a body or building established for research, teaching, or a profession
senses.definitionCN: 为研究、教学或某种专业而建立的机构或场所
senses.example: She works at a small institute studying coastal life.
senses.exampleCN: 她在一家研究海岸生物的小研究所工作。
senses.why: The thing set up became the institution itself: first a purpose, then the body that serves it.
senses.whyCN: 被设立起来的东西变成了机构本身：先有一个目的，再有服务于它的组织。

senses.title: To begin a legal action
senses.definition: to start legal proceedings against someone, in formal usage
senses.definitionCN: 正式用法中，对某人提起诉讼
senses.example: The company instituted proceedings against the supplier.
senses.exampleCN: 公司对供应商提起了诉讼。
senses.why: A case is formally set up before a court, so the same verb covers starting it.
senses.whyCN: 案件在法庭上被正式设立起来，所以同一动词也指「提起诉讼」。

intro.en: Institute comes from Latin instituere "to set up, place in position", built on statuere "to make stand".
intro.cn: institute 来自拉丁语 instituere「设立、安置」，基于 statuere「使之站立」。

items.en: Stare "to stand" and its causative statuere "to make stand, set up" are classical.
items.cn: stare「站立」及其使役形式 statuere「使站立、设立」都见于古典拉丁语。

items.en: In- plus statuere gave instituere, "to set up, undertake, teach".
items.cn: in- 加 statuere 得到 instituere，意为「设立、着手、教导」。

items.en: The noun institutum meant a purpose, a custom, or an arrangement.
items.cn: 名词 institutum 意为「目的、惯例、安排」。

items.en: Old French institut carried the noun into English as a name for a learned society.
items.cn: 古法语 institut 把名词传入英语，指学术团体。

items.en: From the eighteenth century institute names technical and research bodies.
items.cn: 自十八世纪起，institute 被用来命名技术与研究机构。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the standing root and the -stitut- stem; the near-meaning group holds other words for founding and organisations.
note.cn: 形近组共享「站立」词根与 -stitut- 词干；近义组收其他表示「设立」与「机构」的词。

entries.definition: An established organisation or custom, the noun of result.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「机构、制度」，是结果名词。

entries.definition: To make up or form something, with con- meaning together.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「构成」，前缀 con- 表「共同」。

entries.definition: To put one thing in place of another, with sub- meaning under.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「替换」，前缀 sub- 表「在下」。

entries.definition: To set something up permanently, plainer than institute.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「建立」，比 institute 更朴素。

entries.definition: To be the first to start an organisation or city.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「创建」，指最先发起组织或城市。

entries.definition: A learned society or school, a near synonym for the noun sense.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「研究院、学院」，与名词义近义。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the standing root and the double life of the word as noun and verb.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子利用「站立」词根，以及这个词名词、动词两用的特点。

normal.en: in plus statuere: to set something standing, hence to set up.
normal.cn: in 加 statuere：让某物立起来，故为「设立」。

normal.en: Institute is both the act and the building.
normal.cn: institute 既是动作，也是建筑。

normal.en: A research institute institutes its own rules.
normal.cn: 研究所会设立自己的规矩。

normal.en: Same family as constitute and substitute.
normal.cn: 与 constitute、substitute 同族。

normal.en: The noun stress is on the first syllable.
normal.cn: 名词重音在第一音节。

abstract.en: Picture a sign being planted in empty ground.
abstract.cn: 想象在空地上立起一块牌子。

abstract.en: To institute is to give a habit a fixed address.
abstract.cn: 设立就是给一种习惯一个固定地址。

abstract.en: Institutions outlive the people who institute them.
abstract.cn: 机构比设立它的人活得更久。

examples.en: The school instituted a ban on phones in class.
examples.cn: 学校设立了课堂禁用手机的规定。
